label: Sentence-boundary punctuation and line breaks
explanation: Fires on punctuation and whitespace at boundaries: sentence-final periods/question marks, newlines/blank lines, colons before speakers or lists, and often the first token after such a boundary. Strongest when a sentence end is followed by a line break or closing quote (e.g. ".\n", ".”") or a colon introduces a speaker; commas, dashes, spaces, and ordinary words after boundaries give only weak spillover. It does not fire on content words or most mid-clause punctuation.
